tldr: This is a loose cluster of independent projects sharing a label, not one developing event. Omneum opened it on Oct 30 with a local context control plane for agents, and on Nov 4 the vLLM blog introduced Kinference, an open source inference control plane for vLLM on Kubernetes, followed by GitSeed for coding agents on Nov 15.
whats_new: QuadGate, posted to Hacker News on Nov 18, pitches a 4-gate control plane that keeps agent KV prefix caches warm.
why_it_matters: "Control plane" now names four different layers: agent context, coding-agent orchestration, multi-tenant inference serving, and prefix-cache management. Check which layer a tool actually governs before adopting it.

beats.headline: Omneum pitches a local, text-blind context control plane for agents
beats.summary: A Show HN project applying the label to context management for AI agents.

beats.headline: Kinference brings an open source control plane to vLLM on Kubernetes
beats.summary: Token rate limiting, tenant usage and cost tracking, and load balancing for self-run inference platforms.

beats.headline: GitSeed pitches a self-hosted control plane for coding agents
beats.summary: The label returns to open source agent tooling, scoped to AI coding agents.

beats.headline: QuadGate targets warm KV prefix caches for agents
beats.summary: A Show HN project that places a 4-gate control layer between agents and the inference cache.

open_questions: Does Kinference see adoption or contributions beyond its launch post on the vLLM blog?
Does QuadGate publish cache hit-rate or latency numbers, and does it work with vLLM prefix caching?
What does GitSeed actually control for coding agents: sandboxes, permissions, repo access, or just job scheduling?
Does Omneum gain users or contributors after its Show HN post?
take_for_builders: If you run vLLM on Kubernetes, evaluate Kinference for per-tenant rate limits and cost tracking in a staging cluster. Treat Omneum, GitSeed and QuadGate as early experiments until they show releases, benchmarks and outside contributors.
